title: Controlled kNN Connectivity Ablation: Static GCN versus EvolveGCN-H at 500 Universes, Top100 Halos, and Hidden Dimension 64
scientific_question: How does changing the number of periodic-kNN neighbours affect Omega_m prediction performance for Static GCN and EvolveGCN-H under a fixed h64 protocol?

fields_allowed_to_differ.reason: The analysis intentionally compares the EvolveGCN-H and Static GCN architectures.
EvolveGCN-H uses temporal graph sequences; Static GCN uses final-snapshot static graphs.
The established model-specific h64 protocols use batch sizes 4 and 8.
The established h64 protocols use two EvolveGCN-H layers and three Static GCN layers.
Mean temporal pooling applies only to EvolveGCN-H.
Each architecture retains its established regression head.
EvolveGCN-H uses five snapshots while Static GCN uses the final snapshot.
The dataset representation is temporal for EvolveGCN-H and final-snapshot static for Static GCN.
Five temporal snapshots apply only to EvolveGCN-H.
Final-snapshot selection metadata applies only to Static GCN.

controlled_variables_summary: Both model families use the same 500-universe population, Top100 raw-mass node selection, seven node features, minmax normalization, periodic kNN construction in a 25 h^-1 Mpc box, k values, hidden dimension, seeds, and exact ordered split IDs.
limitations_summary: This experiment tests kNN connectivity at hidden dimension 64. It does not establish a universal optimal k, isolate temporal processing causally, or imply generalization to h32.
comparison_statement: Mostly controlled: matched population, graph protocol, k values, hidden dimension, seeds, and exact split IDs, with intentional model and temporal-input differences.
